- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to bullish sentiment.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.4) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if 2+ consecutive days show strong negative sentiment.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast slope in next 5–7 days to allow mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.4–0.6) and price is trending, model often overestimates mean reversion — use 3–5 day smoothing to avoid premature reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum, reduce forecast peak by 5–8% to account for lagged market reaction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), avoid using sentiment as sole driver — weight historical price momentum more heavily than sentiment in correction.
